name: Trippy Figure 8
howto: A trippy spin carried across two objects. Set up as you would for a trippy spin on the first pole, inverted with the object held at the top of the frame, and orbit it. Where the two objects come closest, cross the waist and swap both sticks, so the orbit unwinds and rewinds the other way around the second pole. The ground track comes out as a figure 8, and the reversal at the crossing is what makes it one rather than two orbits flown back to back.
mastery: Link an orbit of each object with a reversal between them.
Even loops either side, the reversal clean and the objects framed.
Continuous figure 8, both objects locked top-center throughout.
steps: Climb inverted up between the two objects
Trippy orbit the first, roll and yaw opposite ways
At the waist, swap both sticks to reverse the spin
Hold the reversed orbit round the second object
Unwind and fly out over the back
prereqs: A solid Trippy Spin either direction
Comfortable reversing a coordinated roll and yaw
practice: Two poles or posts a few metres apart, with clear air around both. Fly a trippy spin on each object on its own first, in both directions, before joining them. The reversal at the waist is the hard part: get it happening at the same place every time, because that is what keeps the two loops even.
mistakes: Reversing early or late, so the loops come out lopsided
Losing the second object while the spin is unwinding
Dropping the inverted hang through the reversal
Objects too far apart to cross the waist without a straight run

name: Trippy Vortex
howto: A trippy spin threaded through a gap. Set the orbit up off to one side of a panel so that one half of every revolution passes through a gap in it and the other half swings round its open edge, then hold the inverted spin and let it sink a little each turn. The gap is the same kind of opening a Ninja Star knife-edges through, turned on its side: wide and short rather than tall and narrow, so the quad can pass through it flat while it orbits. Also called the Trippy Gap.
mastery: Orbit through the gap once and come out still flying.
Two clean turns through the gap, object held in frame.
Continuous sinking spiral, every pass centered in the gap.
steps: Climb inverted into the orbit beside the panel
Trippy orbit round the open edge, roll and yaw opposite ways
Thread the slot on the far side, sinking a little each turn
Unwind and fly out the front
prereqs: A solid Trippy Spin you can hold for two turns
Comfortable putting a quad through a gap without looking at it
practice: Needs a gap you can orbit past rather than just fly through: a doorway, a window, a bando opening, anything with an edge you can swing round on one side. Fly the orbit clear of the gap first and note where the far side of it crosses the opening, because that is the point you have to hit every single turn. Give the gap plenty of margin before you start letting the spin sink.
mistakes: Orbiting too wide, so the pass hits the frame instead of the gap
Sinking faster than the gap is tall, and clipping its lower edge
Losing the inverted hang while the gap is out of frame
Drifting the orbit off centre so only one side lines up
